name: Release a claimed match
description: NOT A FAULT AND NOT A LAPSE. A runner calls this when it cannot play a row -- the usual cause is a model its own roster clock has not registered yet -- and the row goes back to the queue with a refusal spent rather than a strike. The ceiling is what stops a runner that is permanently behind passing one row round the fleet for ever: once the ceiling is spent -- the season's execution.refusal_ceiling, else [vars], the same value the claim sends the runner -- AND the row has waited refusal_grace_secs since it was paired, it fails as MODEL_UNAVAILABLE and says so, which is a diagnosable end. THE GRACE MAKES THE CEILING A MEASURE OF TIME, NOT OF CLAIMS. A new version's first trial is paired before any roster has registered and activated it (two roster ticks at best), trials are claimed first, and a runner's lanes polling every five seconds spend five refusals in seconds -- so a count alone failed rows a roster was about to serve, and charged the failure to the candidate. refusals and lapses are counted apart because they mean different things about the fleet.

with.name: The claim is gone
with.description: Nothing to release means the row was already taken back -- by the reap, or by another attempt. The runner's answer is the same either way: claim again.

tasks.name: Read what became of the row
tasks.description: The runner is told whether its refusal was the one that failed the row, because a refusal that ends a match is worth logging loudly at the edge and an ordinary one is not.

input.query: SELECT json_build_object('released', true, 'refusals', m.refusals, 'failed', m.status = 'failed', 'fault_reason', m.fault_reason) AS body FROM matches m WHERE m.id = ($1)::uuid
